chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: At what amount is the thief's hand cut off? He said: “At a quarter of a dīnār.”
He said: I said to him: For two dirhams? He said: “At a quarter of a dīnār, regardless of whatever value the dīnār may reach.”

He said: So I said to him: What do you think of one who steals less than a quarter of a dīnār? Does the name of thief apply to him when he steals, and is he in that state a thief before Allah? He said: “Everyone who steals from a Muslim something that he has taken possession of and secured, the name of thief applies to him, and before Allah he is the thief. But the hand is not cut off except for a quarter of a dīnār or more. And if the hand of the thief were cut off for what is less than a quarter of a dīnār, you would find most people mutilated.”

key_terms.أَحْرَزَهُ: secured or protected property kept in its safeguarded place
key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the one who commits theft; legally and morally described as a thief
key_terms.حَوَاهُ: taken into possession or enclosed by its owner
key_terms.دِرْهَمَيْنِ: two dirhams, mentioned in contrast to the legal threshold measured by dīnār
key_terms.رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ: the minimum threshold for implementing the hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: the cutting off of the hand as the fixed legal punishment

ai.seo_question: At what amount is the thief's hand cut off in Shia hadith, and is someone still considered a thief if the amount is less than a quarter dīnār?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that the legal hadd punishment for theft applies only when the stolen property reaches a quarter of a dīnār or more. It also distinguishes between the moral and legal meanings of theft: a person who steals less than that is still called a thief before Allah, but the fixed legal punishment is not carried out below that threshold.
